chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn Bukayr asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
About a man who wears a garment in which there is janābah, then he sweats in it, so he said: “Indeed, the garment does not render the man junub.”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام
key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: the garment or piece of clothing under discussion
key_terms.الرَّجُلَ: the man about whom the legal ruling is asked
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةُ: the state of janābah related to major ritual impurity
key_terms.عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ بُكَيْرٍ: a narrator who asks the Imam about the ruling
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: causes someone to become junub or in a state of janābah

ai.seo_question: Does wearing a garment affected by janābah make a person ritually impure?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity and clothing affected by janābah. It states that merely wearing such a garment and sweating in it does not make the person junub, clarifying that janābah is not transferred from the garment to the wearer in this manner.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.151 - Abdullah ibn Bakir asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)

about a man who wears a garment with janabah (ritual impurity from sexual activity) and sweats in it.
Imam (as) said: 'The garment does not make the man ritually impure.'.
